topic: Convergent Plate Boundaries and Landform Formation
key_concepts: Earth's lithosphere is broken into slowly moving tectonic plates.
Three plate boundary types are divergent, convergent, and transform.
Divergent boundaries form mid-ocean ridges and rift valleys.
Convergent boundaries involve plates moving toward each other and form trenches and volcan
Transform boundaries create faults as plates slide horizontally past each other.
The Philippine Sea Plate and Sundaland Plate subduct beneath the Philippine Mobile Belt al
Active volcanoes in the Philippines generally align with trenches.
The Philippine Fault Zone traverses the length of the Philippine Mobile Belt.
Convergent boundaries produce earthquakes, volcanoes, and mountain ranges.
Subduction zone volcanism and mountain building keep continents above sea level.
Convergent boundaries yield resources such as oil, gas, fertile soils, gold, silver, urani
Oceanic-oceanic convergence occurs when an older, cooler, denser oceanic plate subducts.
